newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crudes firm in Asia, Oman believed traded weaker.
newsitem.headline: Crudes firm in Asia, Oman believed traded weaker.

text.p: Crude oil prices held firm in the Asian market on Wednesday staging a modest recovery bolstered by weekly U.S. petroleum data released overnight which showed a decline in U.S. refined products, traders said.
The API data for the week ending April 18 showed a 4.7 million barrel drop to 96.30 million barrels in distillates.
The drop was larger than expected and was seen as a factor to mildly support the market. U.S. crude oil stocks held in primary storage rose roughly 1.4 million barrels to 312.8 million barrels.
June cash Brent was notionally assessed at $18.10/18.15 per barrel in late Tokyo trading.
On SIMEX June Brent was last traded at $18.14 at 0825 GMT, and bid/offered at $18.15/18.20.

In spreads, Brent/Dubai was notionally assessed at $1.45/1.50 for June and $1.50/1.55 for July. The Dubai inter-month spreads were assessed to be in contango with June/July at minus 10/minus 6 and July/August at minus 4/minus 1.
In the physical market, June Oman was widely reported to have traded at a wider discount than the previous deal.
A Japanese trader said it had purchased 100,000 barrels of June Oman at a premium of 75 cents to Dubai.

The trader was believed later to have sold the June Oman as part of a 600,000-700,000 barrel cargo to a Chinese refinery. The June Oman to China was reported to have been traded at a discount of 16.5 cents to the official selling price. The level was lower than the last MPM linked deal believed done at a discount of 15 cents.
A June Dubai was reported to have been sold to a Japanese oil refinery at front-month quotes minus 8 cents. --M.Yoshikawa/Tokyo +81-3-5473-3706/--N.Fullick/Singapore
